data.one_liner: A widget that provides dimensions and offset of a child returned from a builder callback.
data.what_it_does: It measures the width, height, and start offset of a widget rendered inside its builder callback by utilizing render boxes after the first frame. It offers options to rebuild on every frame or listen to dimension updates without rebuilding.
use_when: You need to know the dynamic dimensions or offset of a widget to draw dependent UI elements like lines.
You want to react to size and position changes caused by OS settings.
avoid_when: Standard layout constraints and flexible widgets can already achieve your layout goals without measuring.
You require complex multi-pass layout algorithms where simpler layout widgets would suffice.
strengths: Provides direct access to width, height, and start offset of rendered child widgets.
Includes a listener option to perform actions based on dimensions without interfering with rebuilds.
Supports rebuilding on every frame for tracking dynamic changes.
weaknesses: Relies on measuring after the initial frame, which might introduce layout passes.
Limited to a single specific measurement use case.
